armB_plain.summary: Added API-key authentication to the Task Tracker API's /tasks endpoints. Implemented it as ASP.NET Core middleware (src/TaskTracker.Api/Security/ApiKeyMiddleware.cs) wired in Program.cs before endpoint mapping, so the X-Api-Key check runs ahead of routing, model binding and any handler-level existence/validation logic — an unauthorized caller always gets 401 and never reads or mutates a task. The expected key comes from configuration key "ApiKey", falling back to "test-secret-key"; GET / stays public. Updated the existing test suite to send the key via a CreateAuthenticatedClient() helper and added 11 new cases covering missing/wrong key across all five routes, public root, no-mutation-on-401, and auth-before-validation/existence ordering.
armB_plain.selfAssessment: High confidence. Key design choice: middleware over an endpoint filter, because endpoint filters run after model binding — a malformed/blank body could have produced 400 before 401, violating the "auth before validation" clause. Middleware also covers the {id:guid} route-constraint case. Path matching uses StartsWithSegments("/tasks", OrdinalIgnoreCase), so it protects /tasks and /tasks/* but not a hypothetical /tasksfoo — matches the stated contract. Key comparison is ordinal (case-sensitive), and a header present but empty/whitespace is treated as incorrect. I deliberately did NOT add "ApiKey" to appsettings.json so the documented default path stays exercised. 401 responses have an empty body (no WWW-Authenticate header) — the contract only specified the status code. Also refreshed TaskTracker.Api.http so manual requests still work; that file is non-behavioural. armB_plain.summary: Implemented soft-delete for tasks in the .NET 8 Task Tracker API. armB_plain.summary: Added optimistic concurrency control to PUT /tasks/{id} in the TaskTracker .NET 8 API. TaskItem gained an int Version (serialized as `version`, starting at 1 for new and seeded tasks), UpdateTaskRequest gained an optional ExpectedVersion, and TaskStore.Update now returns a typed outcome (Updated / NotFound / VersionConflict) committed via ConcurrentDictionary.TryUpdate compare-and-swap so a mismatched expectedVersion rejects with 409 Conflict leaving the task fully unchanged, while an omitted expectedVersion keeps last-writer-wins. Added 6 integration tests covering version=1 on create/seed, increments on each successful PUT, matching/stale expectedVersion, and 404 precedence for a missing id.
armB_plain.selfAssessment: High confidence: the contract is small and every clause has a direct test. Two judgement calls worth flagging. (1) The 409 body includes an error message plus expectedVersion/currentVersion — the task only specified the status code, so the body shape is my choice and could differ from an expected fixture. (2) Ordering: a stale expectedVersion against a non-existent id returns 404, not 409, since NotFound is checked first; the task didn't specify this, but 404 seemed correct. Concurrency is handled via TryUpdate CAS with a retry loop rather than a lock; the retry could in principle spin under extreme contention on the unconditional (expectedVersion=null) path, which is acceptable for an in-memory demo store. ExpectedVersion is declared with a `= null` default so the existing 3-field PUT test body still binds. Field naming relies on ASP.NET Core's default camelCase policy (Version -> version, ExpectedVersion -> expectedVersion), which is unchanged in Program.cs.
